 Nearly 6 Million French Press Coffee Makers Recalled Over Risk of ‘Serious Burn Injuries’ 
 Nearly 6 Million French Press Coffee Makers Recalled Over Risk of ‘Serious Burn Injuries’ 
 Here’s how to tell if yours is affected.
 By Jenn Gonick Published: Oct 30, 2026 11:22 AM EDT Save Article Share Article Tony Anderson // Getty Images 2 min read Key Points 
 Popular French press coffee makers are being recalled nationwide, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC).
 The recalled coffee makers may unexpectedly break and potentially cause serious burn injuries.
 Here’s how to tell if yours is affected and what to do if you have one.
 If you like your morning cup of coffee to be a relaxing ritual, a French press coffee maker is the way to go. But if yours is from Bodum, you may want to think twice before starting your next brew—even if you’ve had it for decades. That’s because 5.9 million Bodum French press coffee makers have just been voluntarily recalled nationwide, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC).
 According to the CPSC’s announcement , the coffee makers may be hazardous, as “the carafe can unexpectedly break during use if the glass carafe is damaged or cracked, including by use of a metal spoon to stir the coffee, posing a risk of serious burn injuries.” As of right now, there have already been 70 reports of carafes breaking during use and 48 reports of burn injuries associated with the recall .
 Here’s what you need to know.
 Which products are included in the recall?
 The recall includes a wide variety of Bodum French press coffee maker models with replaceable carafes, dating back to ones manufactured in 1974. Check your kitchen for the following information.
 Bodum 8 oz and 12 oz French press coffee makers with replaceable carafes 
 Add Prevention as a preferred source in your Google search results. Use your Google account to add this to your settings. Add to Google settings Model names: Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper, and Kenya
 Sold in: Retailers including Target, Walmart, and other coffee and home goods stores nationwide, as well as online at Amazon, Target, Walmart, and more
 Sold between: 1974 and October 2026
 More information, including descriptions of the products, can be found in the CPSC’s announcement .
 What should you do with a recalled product?
 If you have one of the recalled French presses in your home, you should first confirm that the carafe isn’t visibly cracked or damaged. The safest thing to do is to not use the coffee maker and throw it away; however, a Bodum representative told CBS News that they aren’t currently issuing refunds to consumers.
 If you do want to continue using your French press (and have confirmed it isn’t damaged), the CPSC says you can “contact Bodum to receive a plastic Bodum stirring spoon and warning label. The label reminds consumers not to use cracked or damaged carafes and not to use metal spoons to stir contents in the glass carafe in order to avoid damaging the glass, which can lead to breakage during use.”
 According to a press release issued by Bodum, changes will come to the French presses following this recall. “Going forward, these products will be sold with the plastic stirring spoon and an additional warning label,” according to the release.
